name: go-invoice
requirements: T1 core/money.go: Money is an amount in cents (int64). ParseMoney(s string) (Money, error) accepts an optional leading -, one or more ASCII digits, and optionally a . followed by one or two digits; it returns an error for anything else, including spaces, a leading + and amounts outside int64. "-0" is 0. String() prints a - for a negative amount, the whole units in decimal without leading zeros (0 below one unit), a . and exactly two digits, so ParseMoney(m.String()) is m. Rate is a nonnegative factor in millionths (int64): 1000000 is 1 and 82500 is 8.25%. ParseRate(s string) (Rate, error) accepts one or more digits, optionally followed by a . and one to six digits, or the same with at most four decimals followed directly by %, which divides it by 100; it returns an error for anything else, including a sign, spaces and values outside int64. Rate's String() formats it as a percentage with at most four decimals, dropping trailing zeros and a trailing ., followed by %, such as 8.25%, 100% or 0%, so ParseRate(r.String()) is r. (m Money) MulRate(r Rate) Money returns m × r ÷ 1,000,000 rounded to the nearest cent, halves away from zero, exactly whenever m × r fits in int64. DivRound(a, b int64) int64 returns a ÷ b rounded to the nearest integer, halves away from zero, and panics when b is 0.

T2 core/model.go and summary.go: LineItem{SKU string; Qty int64; Unit Money; Category string} is Qty units of SKU at Unit each, and its Gross() is Qty × Unit. Invoice{ID, Customer, Currency string; Lines []LineItem} has Subtotal(), the sum of its lines' Gross. Validate() error returns nil for a valid invoice, or an *Error for the first rule it breaks, checked in this order: ID is nonempty and has no whitespace; Customer is not empty or only whitespace; Currency is three ASCII capital letters; there is at least one line; then, line by line, SKU is nonempty, has no whitespace and is not used by an earlier line, Qty is at least 1, Unit is not negative, and Category is nonempty and made only of ASCII lowercase letters, digits and -. Error.Line is the 1-based index of the line at fault, or 0 for the invoice's own fields, including having no lines; Msg is free text. In the root package invoice, Summary starts with ID, Customer string and Subtotal core.Money, and Summarize(inv core.Invoice) Summary returns inv's ID, Customer and Subtotal with every other field zero.

T3 discount/discount.go: ParseRules(text string) ([]Rule, error) reads one rule per line of text, split at \n. Spaces, tabs and \r are trimmed from both ends of each line, blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped, and fields are separated by whitespace. A rule is one of: percent CATEGORY RATE [min QTY] [cap AMOUNT], which takes RATE of the Gross off each line in CATEGORY with at least QTY units (QTY defaults to 1); tier CATEGORY QTY:RATE... [cap AMOUNT], one or more tiers with strictly increasing quantities, which takes off each line in CATEGORY the RATE of its Gross of the last tier whose QTY the line's Qty reaches, and nothing below the first; bundle SKU BUY FREE, which takes Qty ÷ (BUY + FREE), rounded down, × FREE × Unit off the line with that SKU; and off SKU AMOUNT, which takes AMOUNT, but at most Unit, off each unit of the line with that SKU. Optional parts appear in the order shown. RATE is what core.ParseRate accepts, at most 100%; QTY, BUY and FREE are positive integers written only with digits; AMOUNT is what core.ParseMoney accepts, above zero. With a cap, a rule takes at most AMOUNT off a line. Rates apply with Money.MulRate. Any other line returns a nil slice and an *Error whose Line is the 1-based line number; Msg is free text. (r Rule) String() formats a parsed rule as ParseRules reads it, on one line with single spaces: rates by Rate.String, amounts by Money.String, counts in decimal, tiers as QTY:RATE, min only when above 1 and cap only when set, so a rule's String parses back to a rule with the same String. Line(item core.LineItem, rules []Rule) core.Money applies the one rule in rules that takes the most off item: rules never combine, and when none applies nothing is taken off. Whether Line returns the amount taken off or item's price after it (its Gross minus that amount) is the implementer's choice; document the choice in Line's comment.

T4 tax/tax.go: ParseTable(text string) (Table, error) reads a tax table, one entry per line, with discount.ParseRules's line rules (split at \n; trim spaces, tabs and \r; skip blank lines and lines starting with #; fields separated by whitespace). The entries are rate CATEGORY RATE [over AMOUNT RATE2], where lines in CATEGORY whose Unit is above AMOUNT pay RATE2 instead of RATE; default RATE, the rate of categories without a rate entry; and exempt SKU, a SKU that pays no tax. RATE and RATE2 are what core.ParseRate accepts, and AMOUNT is what core.ParseMoney accepts, not negative. A category, the default or an exempt SKU given twice, or any other line, returns a zero Table and an *Error whose Line is the 1-based line number. The zero Table taxes nothing. (t Table) Rate(item core.LineItem) core.Rate returns 0 for an exempt SKU, otherwise the rate of item's category (RATE2 when its Unit is above AMOUNT), otherwise the default rate, otherwise 0. (t Table) Line(item core.LineItem, net core.Money) core.Money returns the tax on item when its price after discount is net: net.MulRate(t.Rate(item)), so tax is rounded per line. (t Table) String() formats t as ParseTable reads it: the default entry if there is one, then the rate entries sorted by category, then the exempt entries sorted by SKU, one per line with single spaces, each ending in \n, rates by Rate.String and amounts by Money.String.

T5 fx/fx.go: ParseTable(text string) (Table, error) reads exchange rates, one entry per line, with discount.ParseRules's line rules. FROM TO RATE means one unit of FROM is worth RATE units of TO: FROM and TO are different codes of three ASCII capital letters, and RATE is what core.ParseRate accepts, above zero and without %. A pair may be given once, in either direction. whole CODE marks a currency without minor units, once per code. Any other line returns a zero Table and an *Error whose Line is the 1-based line number. (t Table) Convert(m core.Money, from, to string) (core.Money, error) returns m unchanged when from equals to. Otherwise it converts along the route of fewest pairs, and among equally short routes the one whose sequence of currencies is alphabetically first, compared currency by currency. A step along a pair as given is m.MulRate(RATE), a step against it is core.DivRound(m × 1,000,000, RATE), and a step into a whole currency then rounds to whole units, a multiple of 100 cents, halves away from zero. With no route it returns an error. (t Table) String() formats t as ParseTable reads it: the whole entries sorted by code, then the pairs as given sorted by FROM and then TO, one per line with single spaces, each ending in \n, rates as decimals without trailing zeros or a trailing .

T6 render/render.go: Table(cols []Column, rows, footer [][]string) string lays out a plain-text table, with Column{Title string; Right bool; Max int}. With no columns it returns "". The title line comes first, then a rule, then the rows; when footer is nonempty, another rule and then the footer rows follow. A row's missing cells are empty, and cells beyond the columns are ignored. A cell's text is split at \n into cell lines, and a row prints as many lines as its tallest cell, at least one. When Max > 0, a cell line, titles included, longer than Max runes is cut to its first Max − 1 runes followed by …. Each column is as wide as its widest cell line, in runes. Each printed line pads every cell line with spaces to its column's width, on the left when Right is set and on the right otherwise, joins them with two spaces and drops trailing spaces; a rule is each column's width in -, joined the same way. Every line ends in \n.

T7 parse/parse.go: Parse(text string) (core.Invoice, error) reads an invoice, one entry per line of text split at \n. A # at the start of a line or after a space or tab starts a comment that runs to the end of the line; then spaces, tabs and \r are trimmed from both ends, blank lines are skipped, and fields are separated by whitespace. invoice ID sets the ID and currency CODE the Currency, each with exactly one field after the keyword; customer NAME sets Customer to the rest of the line, at least one field, with each run of whitespace made one space. Each of these three appears at most once, anywhere in the text. Every other line is an item, SKU QTY UNIT CATEGORY, with QTY written only with digits and fitting int64 and UNIT what core.ParseMoney accepts; items keep their order. Any other line returns a zero Invoice and an *Error whose Line is the 1-based line number. Otherwise Parse returns the invoice and its Validate() result, so Validate reports a missing header. Format(inv core.Invoice) string writes inv as Parse reads it: the invoice, customer and currency lines in that order, then one line per item, with single spaces, QTY in decimal and UNIT by Money.String, each line ending in \n.

T8 totals.go: Totals(inv core.Invoice, rules []discount.Rule, taxes tax.Table) Summary returns Summarize(inv) with three core.Money fields added to Summary: Discount, the sum over inv's lines of the amount rules take off each line; Tax, the sum over its lines of taxes.Line(line, net), where net is the line's Gross minus its discount; and Total, Subtotal − Discount + Tax. Totals does not validate inv.

T9 statement.go: Statement(inv core.Invoice, rules []discount.Rule, taxes tax.Table, rates fx.Table, currency string) (Summary, string, error) returns inv.Validate()'s error, and otherwise any error from converting with rates, with a zero Summary and "". Otherwise its Summary is Totals(inv, rules, taxes) with two fields added to Summary: Currency string, set to currency, and Converted core.Money, set to rates.Convert(Total, inv.Currency, currency). Its text is "Invoice ID for CUSTOMER (CURRENCY)" with inv's ID, Customer and Currency, then \n, then a render.Table with the columns SKU, Qty, Unit, Discount, Tax and Amount, all but SKU aligned right and none with a Max. Each line of inv gives a row, in order: its SKU, its Qty in decimal, its Unit, the amount rules take off it, its tax taxes.Line(line, Gross minus that amount), and its amount, Gross minus the discount plus the tax, with money by Money.String. The footer rows are Subtotal, Discount, Tax and Total, each with its label in the SKU column, the Summary's value in the Amount column and the cells between empty; when currency differs from inv.Currency, a last footer row "Total in CURRENCY" holds Converted. The statement's printed line amounts sum to its printed total.

allocation.A: T1, T3, T4 and T8, with focused tests.
allocation.B: T2, T5, T6, T7 and T9, with focused tests.

dependencies: T3 and T4 use T1's Money and Rate and T2's LineItem.
T5 uses T1. T7 uses T1 and T2.
T8 uses T2's Summarize, T3's Line and T4's Line.
T9 uses T8's Totals, T3's Line, T4's Line, T5's Convert, T6's Table and T1.
T8 and T9 both add fields to Summary in summary.go.
